{'translation': 'Earlier this year, I swapped a battery-powered mower for a robotic mower that I could control with my iPhone. Users have to manually drive the mower around the yard with their iPhone to create a virtual map. Once set up, the robot will automatically perform mowing work according to a preset schedule.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "I've recently tried another system called the TerraMow V1000. It uses a completely different navigation method, and after several weeks of testing, I think for many people it might be the simpler choice.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'Camera-driven automatic map creation', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'The biggest difference between the TerraMow V1000 and the Anthbot M9 I tested earlier this year is how each one understands the yard environment.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'The Anthbot M9 uses RTK base station positioning. During setup, I had to use my iPhone to manually drive the mower along the boundary to create an initial map.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'The TerraMow V1000, on the other hand, uses a system the company calls TerraVision 2.0. Three cameras allow the mower to automatically map the lawn without needing boundary wires laid in advance or an additional RTK antenna installed.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "Automatically creating the initial map takes longer. That said, I think this approach may be easier for users who aren't familiar with tech products.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "To verify this, I specifically asked my mom, who lives in another state, to set up and use the TerraMow V1000 on her own, without my help. She said everything worked well. But I'm not entirely sure she'd have the patience to manually drive the robot around the entire boundary and mark off every area to avoid.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "When the map was being drawn automatically, a small problem showed up in my front yard. There's no fence or other physical divider between my lawn and my neighbour's lawn, so the TerraMow initially included part of the neighbour's lawn in the map.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "I fixed the problem by marking that area as a no-go zone in the app. That said, if the lawn doesn't have a clearly visible boundary, the initial map-drawing process may take a little more effort.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "Viewing through the mower's camera", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "The TerraMow's cameras also support one of my favourite features. The iPhone app can show in real time what the mower sees while it's working.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'During testing, I used the iPhone Mirroring feature on my Mac to open that feed in a larger window. This way I could work indoors while watching the robot, from a first-person perspective, make its way through the back yard.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "This feature isn't necessary for automatic mowing, but it makes using the robot more enjoyable, and every now and then it explains why it slows down or avoids certain objects. The Anthbot M9 has no similar camera-feed feature.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'Beyond that, the two iPhone apps share a lot of similar design elements. Both can schedule jobs, adjust mowing styles, divide zones, mark off areas to avoid, and remotely control the mower.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'Speaking of that last feature, TerraMow has a particularly clever design. In addition to the standard left/right virtual joysticks, its app also offers a one-handed operation mode. You can hold your iPhone as usual and control the mower using just your thumb.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "Manually driving the mower with an iPhone isn't the main purpose of either system. Ideally, the robot should complete the job automatically according to a preset schedule, with no human input. That said, when it comes to tidying up patches the mowing robot missed, TerraMow's joystick control is surprisingly useful.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "Sometimes, I almost feel like I'm controlling the robot with telekinesis (a very strange feeling). I can walk along with my iPhone hanging by my side, and with just a light push of my thumb, the robot will drive over to me.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'Every robotic mower app should emulate this kind of control scheme.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'A more aggressive mower', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'Overall, the TerraMow V1000 feels more aggressive than the Anthbot M9. During testing, it cut lower and was noticeably louder at work.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "I wouldn't say the TerraMow is loud, but the difference between the two is obvious. The Anthbot runs so quietly you can almost forget it's still mowing, even when it's working at night with its headlights on.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'Since the TerraMow relies on camera navigation, it needs daylight to operate reliably. So daytime scheduling becomes more important.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "The V1000 itself feels solid, and it's larger than the Anthbot M9. TerraMow includes a protective garage that can cover the charging station, whereas the Anthbot's garage has to be purchased separately.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "Most importantly, the TerraMow has been completely reliable. I've relied on it to mow for several weeks in a row and have never needed to step in myself.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'When adaptive mapping becomes too clever', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'The visual intelligence that makes TerraMow easy to set up can sometimes backfire.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "The mower continuously updates its map based on what it sees. Saving these updates after each session takes time, during which you can't do anything else in the app.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'After several days of continuous rain, I ran into an interesting situation. Puddles had formed in parts of the yard, and the TerraMow cleverly avoided that area during its next mow.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'The skipped circular patch started growing taller weeds. As time went on, the mower seemed to treat that area of tall grass as somewhere to keep avoiding—even after the ground dried out, that section of lawn remained excluded from its working area.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "I used the app's remote-control feature to manually drive the mower over and trim that patch of tall grass. Once the area returned to a normal lawn state, automatic mowing resumed there as usual.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'Regularly trimming the edges can also help the TerraMow approach boundaries more confidently. If the grass in areas with unclear boundaries grows too tall, the system may mistake it for an obstacle rather than part of the mowing area.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'The Anthbot\'s approach is less adaptive and relies more heavily on user-defined boundaries and obstacles. That method requires more upfront work, but it avoids the situation where a patch of grass causes the map to "change its mind."', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': '9to5Mac take', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "Having tried both systems, for most people I'd lean towards recommending TerraMow's camera-based approach.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'For me, laying boundary wires is completely off the table, and installing an RTK base station also means having to deal with one more piece of hardware that needs positioning, power and maintenance. TerraMow requires neither.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "Its visual navigation isn't perfect. The initial map drawing takes longer, unseen property boundaries need manual correction, and its adaptive behaviour has mistaken tall grass for a permanent obstacle.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "All of these issues are manageable. In return, the TerraMow V1000 offers simpler setup, reliable automatic mowing, high-quality real-time camera feed, and the best manual control I've seen in a robotic mower app.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'Personally, I enjoy working on my yard, but mowing is the most repetitive part. Handing that job over to a robot frees up more time, so I can focus on landscaping, edging and other detail work while still keeping the lawn tidy.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': "The TerraMow V1000 performs well enough to recommend, especially for those who want a robotic mower but don't want the hassle of laying wires, installing an RTK antenna, or walking around the entire yard.", 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'Amazon currently prices the TerraMow V1000 at $999, and the site also offers a $200 coupon. You can also find this product on the TerraMow official website.', 'isOriginal': True}

{'translation': 'Get the most out of your Apple devices', 'isOriginal': True}
